hero.title_html:
The Go-First Software Engineering Ecosystem.
One Ecosystem. Every Workload.
hero.lead_html: Krewire is an end-to-end digital SDLC platform and application ecosystem in Go — spanning the entire software lifecycle from specification, autonomous AI agents, enterprise SSO & RBAC, hybrid PaaS, virtual dev workspaces, to production server operations. Far beyond modular Go libraries, Krewire delivers a cohesive, unified platform driven by a single CLI kiw. Built on three immutable pillars: secure, sustainable, and scalable.
hero.meta: Go 1.27.1+ · Spec to Production · File-based routing · Scoped CSS · Progressive by design

products.title: The Krewire Ecosystem
products.lead: One unified architecture and digital SDLC ecosystem — from autonomous AI workspaces and enterprise IAM to hybrid PaaS and server management.
products.workspace_desc: Virtual workspace & autonomous integration engine. Web terminal, sandboxed runtimes, real-time code collaboration, and deep AI agent automation.
products.cloud_desc: Enterprise hybrid PaaS engine and multi-tenant control plane. Hermetic builds, declarative deployments, process supervision, and edge gateways.
products.auth_desc: Centralized multi-tenant identity and access management. Single Sign-On (OIDC/SAML2), MFA (TOTP), session federation, and hierarchical RBAC.
products.panel_desc: Declarative web, form, and admin panel builder for Go and .kiw. Schema-driven form engine, data table resources, and interactive dashboard studio.
products.panel_feature2: Tabular CRUD resources, pagination & column sorting
products.panel_feature3: Admin panel studio & visual console (kiw forge studio)
products.boundary_note: The open-source core (kiw CLI, libraries, krew, ui) is MIT-licensed and needs none of these services. Dash, Cloud, Auth, and Forge are optional platform services developed in private repositories; none is publicly available yet and no pricing is published.

mission.title: Impact First. Sustainable by Design.
mission.statement: Krewire's mission is to make it nearly free — in financial cost, operational burden, and cognitive effort — for anyone to build, own, and operate digital products that are secure, sustainable, and scalable.
mission.who_desc: Independent developers and small engineering teams first. Learners and educators, open-source maintainers, and organizations benefit from the same open foundation.
mission.impact_desc: Success is long-term impact on how software is built, not revenue. The open-source core needs no account, license key, or Krewire-hosted service.
mission.sustain_desc: Optional platform services may be offered commercially in the future to fund maintenance. Not every service must be free — but the core tooling is never paywalled. No pricing is published today.
mission.vision: Long-term aspiration: a single builder can still read, run, and afford what they built with Krewire a decade from now.

audiences.title: Built for Independent Developers and Small Teams
audiences.lead: Adopt one workload at a time, next to the stack you already have. No full migration required.
audiences.indie_desc: One language, one CLI, and one config file instead of a separate bundler, backend framework, docs generator, and deploy scripts.
audiences.indie_uc1: Publish a landing page or blog → site
audiences.indie_uc3: Ship a small web app or API as one binary → app
audiences.team_desc: Shared conventions and lifecycle commands across services, so moving between them does not mean switching mental models.
audiences.team_uc1: Move slow work out of the request path → worker
audiences.team_uc2: Add a headless service next to an existing app → service
audiences.team_uc3: Deploy to a VPS with systemd → kiw deploy
audiences.secondary: Also relevant to learners and educators, open-source maintainers, and organizations evaluating self-hostable tooling.

pillars.title: Secure. Sustainable. Scalable.
pillars.lead: Krewire is an end-to-end digital SDLC ecosystem — from the first line of the specification to running production. Every capability must pass all three pillars before it ships, and each claim traces to a spec, a test, or a gate.
pillars.secure_desc: Security is a default, not a feature. A stdlib-first dependency graph, secure-by-default HTTP primitives, OWASP/CWE-aligned controls, secrets referenced — never stored — and WASM sandboxing keep the attack surface small and auditable.
pillars.sustainable_desc: Software a single builder can still read, run, and afford a decade from now. Single static binaries with embedded assets, opt-in batteries that cost nothing when unused, boring proven parts, and no license fees — ever.
pillars.scalable_desc: Growth is additive, not a rewrite. The progressive pipeline takes a product from static site to monolith to workers, services, and infra — each stage an opt-in, reversible battery, from a $5 VPS to hyperscale.

workloads.title: One Unified Architecture. Eight Workloads.
workloads.lead: Stop assembling disparate tools for web, CLI, background queues, and infra. Krewire provides unified ergonomics, shared configuration, and zero context switching.
workloads.app_desc: Fullstack web monolith — compile your web interface, HTTP routing, and API handlers into a single static Go binary.
workloads.cli_desc: Developer command-line tools & rich terminal interfaces powered by the lightweight TUI library with zero dependencies.
workloads.site_desc: High-performance static marketing sites, landing pages, and blogs built with the .kiw DSL and scoped CSS styling.
workloads.book_desc: Technical documentation, knowledge bases, and API references compiled with the native pkg/book engine.
workloads.worker_desc: Asynchronous background queues, scheduled recurring tasks, and durable workers with graceful shutdowns.
workloads.service_desc: Headless microservices, JSON REST APIs, and gRPC endpoints engineered for high concurrency and low latency.
workloads.infra_desc: Automated bare-metal and VPS provisioning, TLS certificate issuance, and zero-downtime blue-green deployments.
workloads.gateway_desc: Declarative reverse proxy fronting upstream services with per-route middleware, rate limiting, timeouts, and service-discovery balancing.

steps.title: From Zero to Production in 4 Commands
steps.lead: No boilerplate scaffolding, no package manager wrestling, no hidden magic.
steps.s1_desc: Install the standalone kiw CLI tool via a single-line shell script or Go install.
steps.s2_desc: Generate a production-ready project template for any workload in under one second.
steps.s3_desc: Instant hot-reload local development server with file-based routing and scoped CSS updates.
steps.s4_desc: Compile into a single static binary or static asset bundle and ship to GitHub Pages or Docker.

why.title: Go-First. Progressive. Zero Bloat.
why.lead: Built for engineers who value compilation speed, predictable deployments, and maintainable software architecture.
why.w1_desc: No Node.js, no npm dependencies, and no bundler configuration. Your entire application compiles with standard Go tooling into clean, self-contained binaries.
why.w2_desc: Combines YAML frontmatter, standard Go HTML templates, and scoped <style> blocks. CSS classes never leak outside their component boundary.
why.w3_desc: Start as a lightweight static site, grow into a fullstack web monolith, then seamlessly extract background workers and microservices — all within the same ecosystem.
why.w4_desc: Engineered with production defaults: structured JSON logging, distributed tracing, health checks, circuit breakers, and graceful shutdown out of the box.

dsl.title: Write Pages as Clean .kiw Components
dsl.lead: The elegance of Svelte and Astro brought to Go. Frontmatter + HTML + scoped CSS in one intuitive file.
dsl.f1_html: Scoped by Default: Styles remain strictly isolated to the component.
dsl.f2_html: Global CSS via :root: Theme tokens cascade cleanly across layouts.
dsl.f3_html: Built into kiw: Compiled natively via kiw/dsl with zero npm or external bundler dependencies.
dsl.f4_html: Light & Dark Mode: Native token switching via data-theme.
dsl.scoping_desc: Every .kiw component receives automatic data-kiw-component scope hashing at build time. No CSS collisions, no naming gymnastics, zero runtime cost.

matrix.title: Why Engineers Choose Krewire
matrix.lead: Compare the simplicity of an all-in-one Go toolchain against fragmented multi-language setups.
matrix.row6_trad: Heavy multi-stage Docker containers with Node layers
matrix.row6_krewire: Single self-contained Go binary or static assets

ecosystem.title: Unified Multi-Repo Architecture
ecosystem.lead: The Krewire digital SDLC platform is organized into focused, independent repositories that compose cleanly.
ecosystem.core_desc: Modular Go packages (pkg/*), devtool CLI (kiw), WebAssembly web runtime, ORM, and Boost AI agents.
ecosystem.krew_desc: Autonomous AI agent runtime: in-process embed, standalone CLI, HTTP/SSE transport, and MCP integration.
ecosystem.cloud_desc: Self-hosted PaaS engine, multi-tenant cloud control plane, hermetic builder, and dynamic edge reverse proxy.
ecosystem.auth_desc: Multi-tenant identity, Single Sign-On (OIDC/SAML2), MFA (TOTP), reset password, and hierarchical RBAC.
ecosystem.dash_desc: AI-powered virtual workspace for integration, automation, sandboxed cloud runtimes, and collaborative engineering.
ecosystem.panel_desc: Self-hosted server & admin control panel for bare-metal VPS, vHosts, systemd daemons, databases, and firewall.
ecosystem.internal_desc: Private documentation hub: architecture decision records, roadmaps, contributor guides, and research notes.
ecosystem.portal_desc: Official production website and documentation portal built with site kind & .kiw DSL.
ecosystem.community_desc: Community portal for contributors, releases, guides, and sponsorships.
ecosystem.ui_desc: Composable, zero-dependency .kiw component library and styling system (shadcn model for Go).

cta.title: Start Building with Krewire Today
cta.lead: Start with a lightweight static site, scale to a web monolith, then to distributed cloud services — one repository, one CLI, one configuration.

playground.title: Component Playground
playground.lead_html: Every preview below is a real .kiw component from github.com/krewire/ui, rendered by kiw build for each variant and size. Toggle the options, compare the light and dark themes side by side, then copy the component source or the exact usage snippet. Nothing is fetched from the network.
playground.noscript_html: The live preview needs JavaScript. You can still open the static preview page linked from the component docs.
playground.button_desc: Primary interactive element. Variants map to intent; sizes follow the sm / md / lg scale.
playground.badge_desc: Compact status or category label in seven semantic colours and two sizes.
playground.input_desc: Labelled text field with help text, validation error, and disabled states.
playground.card_desc: Surface container with a title block and a body slot, in four emphasis variants.
playground.modal_desc: Native dialog element. Press the button inside the preview to open it; Esc or the buttons close it.
playground.tabs_desc: Accessible tab list. Click a tab inside the preview to move the active state.
playground.alert_desc: Inline feedback banner for info, success, warning, and error messages.
